parameters.query:
UPDATE traxkey.ordered_items
SET expected_on = {{ $json.newExpectedDate ? "'" + $json.newExpectedDate + "'" : 'expected_on' }},
    status = CASE WHEN '{{ $json.classification }}' = 'received' THEN 'received' ELSE status END,
    received_on = CASE WHEN '{{ $json.classification }}' = 'received' THEN COALESCE({{ $json.newExpectedDate ? "'" + $json.newExpectedDate + "'" : 'NULL' }}, CURRENT_DATE) ELSE received_on END
WHERE id = '{{ $json.recordId }}';

nodes.name: Log Invoice Reply Event
nodes.notes: Deliberately never writes to invoices.status or paid_on here, even for 'claims_paid'. Matches the project rule stated in invoice_chase.py's own docstring: 'TraxKey chases; it never collects.' A self-reported email claim of payment is not proof of payment, marking paid requires a real, separately-verified payment record. This just logs the claim for a human to see and act on.
